newsitem.title: UK: US funds upbeat on stocks amid rate hopes - survey.
newsitem.headline: US funds upbeat on stocks amid rate hopes - survey.

text.p: U.S. fund managers are more bullish about the outlook for U.S. equities as prospects for a hike in interest rates receded, a survey by Merrill Lynch said.
It said bulls on the U.S. equity market outnumbered bears by 30 percent on a three month view -- the highest level since February 1996.

The survey, conducted in the week following the July 2 FOMC meeting which left rates unchanged, said the bullishness was consistent with the improved outlook for Fed Funds, where the average forecast was for an unchanged 5.5 percent against previous expectations of a 0.25 percentage point rise.

"This poll suggests that investor bullishness is highest since February 1996. Wall Street could be susceptible to a sharp pull-back if the Fed does raise rates," said Merrill global strategist Bijal Shah.

The survey said that despite the positive outlook for U.S. equities, investors appeared to prefer investing in overseas equity markets. Of the international markets, respondents were most keen to raise their weighting in Japanese equities.
They were less keen on Latin American equities and positive on continental Europe. They were neutral on UK equities.
U.S. fund managers were on balance looking to reduce their domestic equity exposure, said Shah, due to the relative attraction of overseas markets.
Among U.S. sectors, utilities are unloved, while financials and technology are well liked.
The survey found a lack of interest in domestic bonds and a return to favour of bonds outside the U.S.
The survey, conducted by Gallup, was carried out between July 4 and 9, covering 40 institutions responsible for funds totalling $1.64 trillion.
